speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources whether the Ministry will consider banning the display, slaughter and sale of wild-caught live soft-shelled turtles at the wet markets due to zoonotic disease transmission risks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: This includes ensuring stall cleanliness and proper storage practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Enforcement actions will be taken by SFA against vendors for food safety and hygiene infringements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: SFA has not detected such infringements during its regular inspections.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: SFA, in consultation with NParks and NEA, has evaluated the risk of zoonotic disease transmission by reptiles associated with the slaughter and sale of live turtles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: There have been no cases of zoonotic disease transmission from these animals at the wet market stalls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: In general, food-borne bacteria such as Salmonella can be found in all live animals and raw meat, and these can be transmitted to people through direct contact or ingestion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: To prevent food-borne illnesses, both stall vendors and patrons should observe good food safety and hygiene practices, such as the washing of hands with soap and water before and after handling raw meat, and by thoroughly cooking the meat, which helps to kill any harmful bacteria in food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Members of the public can also report non-compliant wet market stall vendors to SFA or NEA via the agencies’ online feedback forms.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The risk is very similar to what might have led to this whole COVID-19 pandemic in the first place.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These animals are also wild-caught, which means they came from another country and we do not know what diseases they might be carrying.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: From the point of capture to transport, to where they are starved in Singapore, they are terribly stressed, which would weaken their immunity, increase the chance of disease again.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The most important point is, this is not a staple food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, why are we as a Government taking this risk?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Again, bearing in mind what we have gone through with the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, from a human health standpoint, can the Senior Minister of State clarify why we want to take such risks?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, let me say that, currently, there are four stallholders in wet markets managed by NEA, who are selling live turtles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said earlier, we have stopped tendering out wet market stalls for the sale of live turtles since 2012.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: SFA, in consultation with NParks and NEA, has evaluated the risk of zoonotic disease transmission by reptiles associated with the slaughter and sale of live wild-caught turtles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The risk of transmission, as I have said earlier, of pathogens or disease by reptiles such as through the sale and slaughter of live turtles is assessed to be low as long as food safety and hygiene standards are maintained.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And there have been no cases of zoonotic disease transmission from these animals from our wet market stalls.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Also, when we look at the potential human health risks associated with the trade of wildlife, the vast majority of zoonotic pathogens, especially the emerging ones, are associated with mammals and birds rather than reptiles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, in 1992, we stopped the slaughtering of poultry at our wet markets and centralised this at the slaughterhouses.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: SFA's regular inspections have also not detected any food safety and hygiene infringements at these wet market stalls.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But, as I had also earlier said, the agencies are reviewing the sale and slaughter of live animals at our wet market stalls, taking into consideration international benchmarking and scientific evidence, and also as part of our efforts to improve food safety and environmental hygiene standards in Singapore, including at the wet markets.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As part of this review, we will consult the relevant stakeholders and we will share of the outcome of this review when ready.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Why is it that we have one agency, NParks, that says that actually, we cannot keep these turtles as pets because of a disease transmission concern; and all of a sudden, that disease transmission concern disappears when it comes to the wet market?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, can we align the views of the two agencies and to synchronise them?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Second, I just want to share that the Salmonella infections can actually be fatal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, it is not a thing that we can just brush aside.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But if you get the Salmonella infection from the turtles, it can actually kill you.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The other point about SFA and NParks, even for the sale of live turtles, both SFA and NParks are involved.
